answer: In an agent market for ferrous scrap, each seller must lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before its offers enter search results, with one active offer per bond. An attacker trying to mirror a busy market with 10,000 fake sellers must immobilize $1 million; creating more keys buys no extra visibility without more deposits. Even at the nadir of trading activity, the lock persists, making a sustained sybil swarm costly in tied-up capital.
